security.gate: Issue, focused CI, rollback evidence, human merge
security.route: expedited Change; never direct production mutation

patch.gate: compatibility tests, lock regeneration, human merge
patch.route: catalog Change or project Change as ownership requires

minor.route: catalog Change plus project adoption Change

major.gate: migration, backup, restore and rollback plan

components.name: Ubuntu Server LTS

provenance.evidence: Canonical release notes give exact standard security maintenance through 31 May 2029; the release table lists 24.04.4 and April 2039 EOL, normalized to the final calendar day.

compatibility: Docker Engine official packages support Ubuntu 24.04 on amd64 and arm64.
Production image and apt repository snapshots require checksums/signature verification.
components.remediation: Remain on the pinned 24.04 point release until a later LTS passes a separate compatibility Change.

components.name: Ubuntu Server LTS

provenance.evidence: Canonical lists 26.04 LTS, but the platform has no post-point-release compatibility and soak evidence yet.

compatibility: Docker documents Ubuntu 26.04 package availability.
Catalog approval remains blocked until first point release plus AISoftPlatform soak evidence.
components.remediation: Create a separate OS adoption Change after 26.04.1 and complete rollback-capable compatibility testing.

components.name: Windows Server

provenance.evidence: Microsoft Lifecycle lists Windows Server 2025 mainstream and extended support dates; build 26100 is recorded in the official container base-image table.

compatibility: IIS is pinned as an OS feature manifest, not an independently serviced semver package.
.NET hosting bundle must match the selected .NET major.
components.remediation: Use the approved OS media/build and reviewed Windows feature manifest; do not infer IIS servicing separately.

components.name: Node.js

provenance.evidence: Node.js official release table identifies v24 as LTS through April 2028; Context7 official docs identify 24.18.0 as the current v24 patch.

compatibility: Prisma 7 supports Node ^24 and requires an LTS Node release.
npm 11 supports Node >=22.9 and is compatible with Node 24.
components.remediation: Pin the exact runtime and package-manager versions in the project declaration and application lock.

components.name: Node.js

provenance.evidence: The official archive verifies exact v22.22.3; the release schedule places v22 in Maintenance LTS through April 2027. Context7 identifies a newer v22 patch, so this approved transition fact is exact but is not described as latest.

compatibility: Prisma 7 supports Node ^22.12, but adoption still requires a separate ORM migration.
Existing projects require a migration Issue and may not combine runtime and database majors without separate gates.
components.remediation: Open a project Change for Node 24 and reference it from the declaration before adopting this sunset entry.

components.name: npm CLI

provenance.evidence: npm CLI v11 official docs identify 11.19.0 and supported Node engine ranges; npm publishes no fixed EOL schedule.

compatibility: Use npm ci so package-lock and package.json mismatch fails.
Pin packageManager/devEngines and mirror package tarball integrity metadata.
components.remediation: Review quarterly because upstream does not publish a fixed EOL date.

components.name: npm CLI

provenance.evidence: Official npm v10 changelog records 10.0.0; registry metadata pins its integrity and Node engine range. npm publishes no fixed v10 EOL, so 2027-01-31 is an AISoftPlatform transition deadline, not an upstream support promise.

compatibility: npm 10.0.0 supports Node ^18.17 or >=20.5, including the pinned Node 22 transition runtime.
A project must pin packageManager and package-lock integrity; a semver range is not an architecture identity.
components.remediation: Track npm 11 adoption independently and expire the temporary npm 10 exception no later than 2027-01-31.

components.name: Prisma ORM

provenance.evidence: Official Prisma release and v7 upgrade documentation; upstream publishes no fixed EOL date for this line.

compatibility: Requires Node ^20.19, ^22.12 or ^24 and TypeScript >=5.4.
Prisma 7 uses prisma-client with an explicit output path and a database driver adapter.
components.remediation: Treat Prisma 5 to 7 as an independent migration with generated-client, config and adapter tests.

components.name: Prisma ORM

provenance.evidence: Official final v5 release evidence; Prisma provides no fixed v5 EOL table, so dates are AISoftPlatform exception deadlines, not an upstream support promise.

compatibility: Existing prisma-client-js declarations differ materially from Prisma 7 generation and adapter contracts.
No project may infer support beyond the catalog exception deadline.
components.remediation: Create a Prisma-only migration Change and expire any temporary exception no later than 2027-02-02.

components.name: PostgreSQL

provenance.evidence: PostgreSQL Global Development Group lists 18.4 and final support date 2030-11-14; current minor is always recommended.

compatibility: Prisma 7 and Npgsql EF Core require project compatibility tests against PostgreSQL 18.
Major upgrade requires dump/restore or pg_upgrade evidence and a separate database Change.
components.remediation: Adopt only through a database-specific Change with backup, restore and rollback gates.

components.name: PostgreSQL

provenance.evidence: Official supported-version table lists current minor 16.14 and final support date 2028-11-09.

compatibility: Valid for existing projects when exact minor and immutable image identity are verified.
Upgrade to PostgreSQL 18 remains an independent database Change.
components.remediation: Apply current minors and schedule a separate major migration before 2028-08-31.

components.name: SQLite

provenance.evidence: SQLite official change log lists 3.53.3; upstream has no fixed release EOL schedule.

compatibility: WAL requires all processes on one host and does not work over network filesystems.
SQLite permits concurrent readers but only one writer; online backup must be paired with restore drills.
components.remediation: Use only for the small embedded profile and reassess when concurrency, capacity or availability exceeds its limits.

components.name: Docker Engine

provenance.evidence: Docker official install documentation exposes exact stable package versions and currently documents Engine 29.7.1; no fixed EOL schedule is published.

compatibility: Official Ubuntu package support includes 24.04 and 26.04.
Repository metadata and packages must be mirrored and verified before offline import.
components.remediation: Pin exact engine packages; review upstream security releases monthly.

components.name: Docker Compose

provenance.evidence: Official Compose release includes checksum, provenance and SBOM assets; no fixed EOL schedule is published.

compatibility: Use config --resolve-image-digests or equivalent release tooling to capture immutable images.
Compose plugin and Docker Engine combinations require reference-project smoke tests.
components.remediation: Mirror the signed/checksummed plugin asset and reject mutable production images.

components.name: NGINX stable

provenance.evidence: NGINX official download page lists 1.30.4 as stable; upstream publishes no fixed EOL date for the stable line.

compatibility: Stable, not mainline, is the default profile selection.
Package or OCI identity must be immutable and security advisories reviewed monthly.
components.remediation: Use the stable line and handle security releases through the expedited Change path.

components.name: .NET LTS Runtime and SDK

provenance.evidence: Official .NET release metadata records runtime 10.0.9, SDK 10.0.301, active LTS and 2028-11-14 EOL.

compatibility: ASP.NET Core and EF Core must use the same major version.
Windows IIS hosting bundle must match the .NET 10 major and patch servicing policy.
components.remediation: Service runtime, SDK and hosting bundle together; a major change requires a separate application Change.

components.name: .NET SDK

provenance.evidence: Official .NET release metadata records SDK 10.0.301 with runtime 10.0.9 in the active .NET 10 LTS channel.

compatibility: Build SDK 10.0.301 produces applications for the pinned .NET 10 runtime.
The build environment pins the SDK separately from the production runtime and hosting bundle.
components.remediation: Update SDK and runtime servicing pins together after official metadata and build parity review.

components.name: ASP.NET Core Runtime

provenance.evidence: Official .NET metadata records ASP.NET Core runtime 10.0.9 in the .NET 10 LTS channel.

compatibility: Must remain major-aligned with .NET runtime and EF Core.
IIS in-process hosting does not support single-file deployment; use a reviewed folder or out-of-process deployment.
components.remediation: Align all Microsoft framework components on major 10 and validate the IIS hosting model.

components.name: Entity Framework Core

provenance.evidence: Microsoft EF Core documentation ties EF Core major support to the matching .NET major; patch is aligned to the verified .NET servicing release.

compatibility: EF Core providers typically do not work across major versions.
Use Npgsql.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL major 10 for PostgreSQL.
components.remediation: Keep EF Core and every provider on the same major and run migration SQL review in the project Change.

components.name: Npgsql Entity Framework Core provider

provenance.evidence: Official NuGet package metadata for Npgsql EF Core provider 10.0.3; lifecycle follows required EF Core major compatibility rather than a separate upstream schedule.

compatibility: Major 10 is selected for EF Core 10 compatibility.
PostgreSQL 18 compatibility must be proven by project integration tests before adoption.
components.remediation: Pin the package and test translated SQL, migrations and database restore on the selected PostgreSQL major.

components.name: Internet Information Services role

provenance.evidence: Microsoft documents Web-Server as a Windows Server role; servicing and lifecycle inherit the pinned Windows Server build rather than an independent IIS package lifecycle.

compatibility: Install only the reviewed Web-Server feature manifest.
ASP.NET Core Module V2 arrives through the matching hosting bundle and requires hosting-model validation.
components.remediation: Inventory the OS build, enabled feature manifest and hosting bundle together; never infer a standalone IIS patch version.

components.name: Next.js

provenance.evidence: Vercel's July 2026 official security release names 16.2.11 as Active LTS; Context7 v16.2 compatibility docs require Node >=20.9, React >=18.2 and TypeScript >=5.1. No fixed EOL date is published.

compatibility: Node 24, React 19 and TypeScript 6 satisfy documented minimum versions, but project build/browser tests remain mandatory.
A Next.js 14 to 16 migration uses the official codemod guidance and remains independent from Node, Prisma and PostgreSQL major Changes.
components.remediation: Apply Active LTS security patches promptly; perform a 14-to-16 framework migration in its own application Change.

components.name: Next.js

provenance.evidence: Vercel's official support policy marks 14.x unsupported; the dates reflect the published two-year major-version support window. Registry metadata verifies exact package 14.2.33 and its Node >=18.17 and React ^18.2 peer constraints, but exact availability does not make an unsupported line adoptable.

compatibility: NewEmaint remote main resolves Next.js 14.2.33 and React 18.3.1, but Next.js 14 is outside upstream support.
This entry is evidence-only and cannot be placed in a profile transition allowlist or a current architecture lock.
components.remediation: Create and complete an application-owned Next.js migration to a supported major before producing a current release lock.

components.name: React

provenance.evidence: React official documentation identifies 19.3 as the latest stable line; React publishes no fixed EOL schedule.

compatibility: Framework-specific support, such as Next.js peer compatibility, must be validated in the project Change.
Use an exact package lock and offline integrity metadata.
components.remediation: Do not upgrade a framework solely because the catalog has a newer React preferred entry.

components.name: React

provenance.evidence: React's official changelog records 18.3.1 as the final 18.3 release and a bridge toward React 19. React publishes no fixed v18 EOL, so 2027-01-31 is an AISoftPlatform transition deadline, not an upstream support promise.

compatibility: Next.js 14.2.33 accepts React ^18.2, and NewEmaint's lock resolves 18.3.1 in apps/web.
React 18 transition approval cannot override a prohibited framework component in the same application lock.
components.remediation: Migrate React with a supported framework major and expire any temporary exception no later than 2027-01-31.

components.name: TypeScript

provenance.evidence: TypeScript official 6.0 release documentation and Context7 current package metadata identify 6.0.2; no fixed EOL schedule is published.

compatibility: Prisma 7 requires TypeScript >=5.4.
TypeScript 6 deprecations require an application compiler check before adoption.
components.remediation: Run the application typecheck and framework compatibility suite before changing the project declaration.

components.name: TypeScript

provenance.evidence: Official TypeScript 5.8 release documentation and registry metadata verify exact 5.8.3. TypeScript publishes no fixed 5.8 EOL, so 2027-01-31 is an AISoftPlatform transition deadline, not an upstream support promise.

compatibility: TypeScript 5.8.3 satisfies Prisma 5.22 and Next.js 14 compiler requirements observed in NewEmaint.
The project must pass its exact typecheck and framework build before any current adoption.
components.remediation: Move to the preferred TypeScript major within the supported framework migration and before the exception deadline.

components.name: Docker Official Image node bookworm-slim

provenance.evidence: Docker official registry manifest inspection returned the multi-platform index digest and upstream docker-node revision 303e6c3b.

compatibility: The index contains linux/amd64, linux/arm64/v8 and linux/ppc64le manifests plus attestations.
Production identity must retain both the human-readable tag and this sha256 digest.
components.remediation: Import the manifest and attestations into the offline mirror, verify digest and SBOM, then reference the digest in the project declaration.

components.name: Docker Official Image node bookworm-slim

provenance.evidence: Docker Official Image registry inspection for node:22.22.3-bookworm-slim returned multi-platform index sha256:e21fc383b50d5347dc7a9f1cae45b8f4e2f0d39f7ade28e4eef7d2934522b752 and linux/amd64 child manifest sha256:16d364eebf6b62da439dc993d9b80940c78b0ca38438452f011ab9a25c752644. The platform pin is the architecture-specific child digest.

compatibility: This catalog identity is valid only for linux/amd64; a multi-platform index digest cannot substitute for the selected child manifest.
The paired runtime.node.22 transition remains Maintenance LTS and requires its own exception and migration Issue.
components.remediation: Import and verify the linux/amd64 manifest and attestations, then migrate to the preferred Node 24 image before 2027-01-31.
